claim: DATE 1, COMPOSITION. When the hymns were composed. Not attested by anything. No Rigvedic hymn carries a date, no external document dates one, and no excavated object is inscribed with one. Every figure in circulation is inferred from a comparison, and the inference is what carries the weight, not the text.
locator: the pinned corpus itself: no date field exists in strata.json, aufrecht.csv, padapatha.csv, vnh.csv, stanza_properties.json or addressees.json, and none is offered anywhere in TEI/vedaweb_corpus.tei
notes: Typed under the negative-evidence standard as NOT PRODUCED: a Rigvedic hymn is not the kind of document that records its own date, so its absence is not informative about anything. This row exists so that the other seven dates cannot be silently substituted for it.

claim: DATE 2, ORAL CIRCULATION BEFORE FIXATION. The interval between composition and the point at which the text stopped changing. Not measured here and not measurable from the retrieved bundle. Its LOWER bound is zero and no upper bound is established.
locator: no measurement in 04-AUDITS/domain-a-tables/ bears on it; the tables measure differences between transmitted forms, which are evidence that change occurred, not evidence of when it stopped
notes: Constitution 4.A's 'natural oral change before canonical fixation'. DA-M-015 to DA-M-019 show the corpus carries the residue of such change; they do not date it. Recorded as HYPOTHESIS so that no later unit reads the 72% figure as a duration.

claim: DATE 3, COLLECTION AND CANONICAL ARRANGEMENT. When the hymns were ordered into the ten-mandala shape the bundle transmits. Distinct from composition, and the arrangement is what a book number is a fact about. Not established here.
locator: the corpus is delivered pre-arranged; nothing in the retrieved bundle dates the arrangement, and Oldenberg 1888, the standard analysis of it, is not retrieved (HOLD-008)
notes: Constitution 4.A's 'compilation and canonical organization'. This is the date a mandala number belongs to. DA-M-003 measures that book order and Arnold's strata do not co-vary, which is what one would expect if they are facts about two different dates.

claim: DATE 4, FIXATION OF THE SAMHITAPATHA. When the continuous recited text took the form Aufrecht prints. Not established here. It is later than date 2 by construction and earlier than date 5.
locator: versions/aufrecht.csv carries no date; the TEI header gives the modern edition, not the fixation event
notes: Constitution 4.A's 'Samhita transmission'. The Samhitapatha is the object the phonology measured at DA-M-015 to DA-M-018 sits on.

claim: DATE 5, THE PADAPATHA ANALYSIS. When Sakalya's word-by-word analysis was made. Later than date 4, because it analyses it. Not established here; the padapatha in the bundle carries no attribution date.
locator: versions/padapatha.csv and versions/lubotsky.csv; DEP-003 already records what the padapatha can and cannot disambiguate
notes: Constitution 4.A's 'Padapatha and other recitational analysis'. DA-M-018 measures how far the two forms diverge; it does not date either.

claim: DATE 6, PANINI. When the grammarian described Vedic forms under his chandasi rules. Later than dates 4 and 5. NOT ESTABLISHED IN THIS REPOSITORY AT ALL: no edition, translation or study of Panini has been retrieved in any session, and no rule has been read.
locator: full-tree search of this repository: no Panini source in 02-SOURCES/access-ledger.csv and no Panini claim in any register
notes: Constitution 4.A asks what the chandasi rules imply. Nothing in this record answers it, and this row says so rather than supplying a summary from memory. HOLD-008. The trap the constitution names - 'Panini rewrote the Rigveda' - cannot be tested here in either direction.

claim: DATE 7, MANUSCRIPT COPYING. When the surviving physical witnesses were written. Not established here. The bundle transmits printed editions (Aufrecht, van Nooten and Holland, Eichler), not manuscripts.
locator: SRC-078's own blocking_constraint already records that vnh is an editorial reconstruction and not a manuscript witness; the same holds for aufrecht.csv
notes: Recorded because a repository whose whole Rigvedic evidence base is a git clone of printed editions has no manuscript date at all, and should not be able to imply one.

claim: DATE 8, MODERN SCHOLARLY INTERPRETATION. When the instruments used to date the text were themselves made. These ARE attested, exactly, and they are the only dates in this list that are: Grassmann 1876-7, Oldenberg 1888 and 1909/1912, Arnold 1897, Arnold 1905, Wuest 1928, van Nooten and Holland 1994, Witzel 1995, the Cologne and Zurich annotation 2020, Hellwig, Scarlata and Widmer 2021.
locator: TEI/vedaweb_corpus.tei, biblFull xml:id=strata, strata_src, stanza_properties and stanza_properties_src, quoted in 02-SOURCES/vedaweb-manifest-2026-09-09-domain-a.md; SRC-105 for the 2021 date
notes: The one column of this table where every cell is a fact. It is also the shortest span: the entire apparatus by which this repository knows anything about Rigvedic chronology was made between 1876 and 2021, and its chronological core was made in 1905.
